newsitem.title: UK: Expectations rise of broad EMU - JP Morgan index.
newsitem.headline: Expectations rise of broad EMU - JP Morgan index.

text.p: Market expectations of a broad-based European Monetary Union rose further over the past week as Europe finalised its agreement on a post-EMU budget stability pact, JP Morgan's EMU calculator showed.
These expectations, derived from prevailing market prices, rose particularly sharply in Spain to the extent that the market now puts the probability of the peseta being part of EMU at 84 percent.
The U.S. investment house's method of calculating market expectations of EMU taking place monitors bond yield spreads in the swaps market between Germany and other participating European countries.

The latest calculations show that the market's probability of Spain participating in EMU rose 10.0 percentage points to 84 percent in the five trading days to Friday, while perceived EMU probability in Italy rose 5.0 points to 70 percent. Sweden was up two points to 74 percent.

EMU expectations in these three countries have shown a steady rise over the past 20 days, with Spain's probability up an accumulated 27 points over that period, Sweden is up 13 points and Italy is up nine points.

Elsewhere, perceived probability levels in the U.K. rose one point to 39 percent over the last week and were up five points in the last 20 days. While Denmark was up one point last week, however, it weas down six points to 46 percent over 20 days.
According to these calculations, the market still believes there is a 100 percent chance France and Belgium will be in EMU and that was unchanged from last week.

The calculator works by assigning a market probability level to each country. This is derived from the actual swap spread, an in-house assumption of what the spread would be if EMU were not a factor and the expected spread after EMU participation, which is zero.
